overreach: For Anritsu comparisons, verify frequency range, bandwidth, data rate, option code, software tools and support model ... because the Anritsu page says the current weakness narrative is based only on an R&S internal battle card [93].

For Anritsu MX844030PC / Virtual Signalling Tester claims, cite the Anritsu brochure-derived passages only for what they state, such as MX844030PC being Virtual Signalling Tester NR Software with MAC-IF, PHY-IF Digital-IQ and RF-IF configurations [64][85].

Do not claim Anritsu test-case coverage, conformance status or throughput metrics from the Virtual Signalling Tester source, because that source does not provide a full test case list, scenario library, 3GPP release coverage, conformance status or throughput metrics [88].

For conformance, PTCRB, GCF, operator acceptance or validated test-case claims, provide accreditation evidence, validation reports, test package option codes, test case lists, PTCRB / GCF versions and dates where applicable [3][37].

For market share or competitor market-positioning claims, provide third-party market data or official sources, because internal statements about competitor market position or market share are marked as unverified internal sales statements [23][97].
review.reason: The main recommendation to use formal R&S specifications/features documents and official competitor or third-party evidence is well supported by the cited passages. However, several detailed requirements rely on citation numbers whose passage text is not provided here, so those specific claims go beyond the available evidence.
